articles.title: Eastern Michigan vs Central Michigan: Eagles Get Steamrolled 35-7 at Ford Field
articles.byline: Imogen Tremblay, The Eastern Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Central Michigan Chippewas (4-5) 35, Eastern Michigan Eagles (4-6) 7, Wed., Nov. 4, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: at Western Michigan, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo
articles.text:
I'm not going to dress this one up. Central Michigan 35, Eastern Michigan 7, Wednesday night at Ford Field, in a game where we were the home team. We did the Eagle Walk at Brush Street and Adams Avenue, we brought the buses down from Ypsilanti, we tried to turn Detroit green. Then the Chippewas took the ball and kept it.

Here's the damage, straight off the stat sheet. Nine first downs. 177 yards of offense. 74 yards rushing on 21 carries. We went 1-10 on third down. We had the ball for 19:04 while they had it for 40:56. Mitten Football noted we didn't get our second first down until about 10 minutes were left in the game. That's not a slump. That's a stall.

Brogan McCaughey took the first snap and went 12 of 17 for 59 yards with an interception. Amareon Blue had 42 yards on 8 carries. Nobody could get going, and the guys up front got whipped all night.

Meanwhile CMU's Nick Woodford ran for three scores, and their third-quarter drive went 16 plays and 90 yards and ate 8:39. I watched our defense stand on that field so long they needed a change of address.

Credit where it's due. Bryce Llewellyn fought like crazy with 10 tackles, a sack and a tackle for loss. Bryce Eliuk made 10 tackles too. Daniel Hull boomed five punts for a 49.2 average, which tells you how often he was out there. Harold Mack caught a 6-yard touchdown with 10 seconds left to wreck the shutout, and good for him.

But we fell to 4-6, 3-3 in the MAC, and the math is simple now. Two games left, at Western Michigan and home against Kent State. Win both, get to six wins, go bowling. Lose either, and it's wait till next year.

Kalamazoo, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 7 PM ET. It's Western. If that doesn't light a fire in this locker room, we have bigger problems.

articles.title: Central Michigan vs Eastern Michigan: Woodford Scores Three as the Chips Run Through the Eagles in Detroit
articles.byline: Brynn Haverkamp, The Central Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Central Michigan Chippewas (4-5) 35, Eastern Michigan Eagles (4-6) 7, Wed., Nov. 4, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: vs Sacramento State, Wed., Nov. 11, 7:30 PM ET, Mount Pleasant
articles.text:
Forty minutes and 56 seconds. That's how long Central Michigan had the football Wednesday night at Ford Field. Eastern Michigan got the other 19 and change and went nowhere with it. Central Michigan 35, Eastern Michigan 7. Three-game losing streak, gone. We're 4-5, 2-3 in the MAC, and the in-state bragging rights ride back up to Mount Pleasant.

This was a beatdown from the opening drive. Jadyn Glasser hit Justin Ruffin Jr. for 34 to get us rolling, then found Nasir Williams from 8 yards out. 7-0 before the Eagles touched it. Glasser finished 14 of 19 for 175, and he didn't throw one away to them. Neither did anybody else. Zero giveaways.

Then it was Nick Woodford's night. Woodford from 11 to cap a 12-play, 86-yard march. Woodford from 2 right before the half, 21-0. Woodford from 1 in the third, one snap after he ran 12 yards to the doorstep. Three scores, 123 yards on 21 carries. Bell cow.

That third-quarter drive was the knockout. Sixteen plays, 90 yards, 8:39 off the clock. Eastern stood there and watched. We went 5-5 on fourth down and 7-15 on third. When you convert like that, the other team's offense becomes spectators.

And the defense? Nasty. Eastern finished with 177 yards and 9 first downs. Jaion Jackson intercepted Brogan McCaughey in the second quarter. Mayson Hitchens stuffed them on a fourth down in the fourth. We outgained them 418-177 and ran for 235. The shutout died with 10 seconds left, and I'm still annoyed about it.

One gripe: we left points on the field early with a missed 52-yarder. That's it. That's the whole list.

This was our second straight win against Eastern, and the Chippewas' 12th game ever at Ford Field, per CMU Athletics. Next Wednesday, Sacramento State comes to Mount Pleasant at 7:30 PM ET. Two more wins gets us to six. Keep running the ball down people's throats and let's go get them.

articles.title: Sacramento State vs Toledo: Hornets Push MAC Contender to the Final Snap, Fall 20-17
articles.byline: Mateo Villaseñor, The Sacramento State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Toledo Rockets (7-2) 20, Sacramento State Hornets (2-8) 17, Wed., Nov. 4, Hornet Stadium, Sacramento. Next: at Central Michigan, Wed., Nov. 11, 7:30 PM ET, Mount Pleasant
articles.text:
Fourth-and-14, 55 seconds to work with, the ball in Brian Salazar Jr.'s hands, and it got knocked to the turf. That's how the home season ended for the Hornets. Toledo 20, Sacramento State 17. We're 2-8, 1-6 in the MAC, and I'm proud and ticked off in equal parts.

Proud first. Toledo is 7-2 and tied for second in this league, and we had them down 10-7 at halftime. Jackson Sharman went 8 of 15 for 113 and hit Matt Coleman from 2 yards out to cap a 10-play drive. Raiden Brown went up and got a 59-yard ball that bounced off a Toledo defender, which set up Grant Meadors from 38. Brown finished with 5 catches for 108.

The defense hit people too. Boogsie Silvera intercepted John Alan Richter in the first quarter, and Toledo threw for 60 yards the whole night. Tim Thomas had 7 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. Fata Puloka made 8 stops.

Now the ticked-off part. We ran it 31 times for eight yards. Eight. You can't win a football game like that against anybody, let alone a team that rams the ball down your throat for 230. Their two backs both topped 100. We gave Toledo a short field on our first possession with a strip-sack at our own 32, and they scored five plays later.

And the guys still didn't quit. Down 20-10 with 7:51 left, Jamar Curtis capped a 12-play, 75-yard drive from the 3 with 2:20 to go. The defense got the ball back. We just ran out of room from our own 16.

Credit to the seniors who played their last game in Sacramento, and to the new uniforms and hand-painted helmets made with the Wilton Rancheria tribe for Native American Heritage Month. Sharp look, and the effort matched it.

Next Wednesday it's a flight across the country to Mount Pleasant to face Central Michigan, 7:30 PM ET. Find a running game somewhere between here and Michigan, boys.

articles.title: Toledo vs Sacramento State: Miller and Ison Grind Out 20-17 and Keep the MAC Race Alive
articles.matchup: Final: Toledo Rockets (7-2) 20, Sacramento State Hornets (2-8) 17, Wed., Nov. 4, Hornet Stadium, Sacramento. Next: vs Massachusetts, Wed., Nov. 11, time TBA, Glass Bowl, Toledo
articles.text:
Eight yards. Sacramento State ran the ball 31 times Wednesday night and gained eight yards. Toledo Athletics says that's the fewest any Rocket opponent has managed since 2015. That's the story of Toledo 20, Sacramento State 17, and it's why we're flying home from California at 7-2 and 4-1 in the MAC.

Don't let the final fool you. This was not pretty. It wasn't. We trailed 10-7 at the half. John Alan Richter threw for 60 yards all night and threw an interception. Ugly. We went 5-15 on third down. Ugly again.

So we did what Toledo does. We handed it to CJ Miller and Autavius Ison and told them to go get it. Miller carried 27 times for 135 yards. Ison went for 101 on 15 carries, and his 19-yard run late in the third put us up 17-10 for good. Two backs, two hundreds, 230 yards on the ground. That's grown-man football.

The defense set the tone from the first series. Andrew Zock strip-sacked Jackson Sharman, Nathaniel Chandler fell on it at their 32, and five plays later Richter found Anthony Simpson for an 18-yard score. Toledo Athletics counted 12 tackles for loss and five sacks. Isaac Zay made 11 tackles. Chandler had a sack, two tackles for loss and the recovery.

Special teams pulled their weight too. Markus Meincke pinned them inside their own 5 to open the second half, we got the ball back at midfield, and Reice Griffith tied it from 34. He added a 40-yarder for 20-10 with 7:51 left.

I'll admit the last two minutes made me sweat. The Hornets went 75 yards for a touchdown with 2:20 left, then got it back at their own 16. Then our guys sacked Salazar, and on fourth-and-14 the throw got knocked down. Ballgame.

Toledo Athletics says we're tied with Western Michigan and Buffalo for second in the MAC with three to play. Next Wednesday, UMass comes into the Glass Bowl. Same recipe: feed the backs, squeeze the throat, go home happy.

articles.title: Ball State vs Massachusetts: One Missed Kick, a 31-30 Loss and a Long Ride Home
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ball State Cardinals (3-6) 30, Massachusetts Minutemen (5-4) 31 (OT), Wed., Nov. 4, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst. Next: vs Buffalo, Wed., Nov. 11, 7:30 PM ET, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie
articles.text:
One kick. We came into Amherst, punched UMass in the mouth for four quarters, scored first in overtime, and then the extra point sailed wide left. Watson ran 13 yards on the other end, they made their kick, and Ball State lost 31-30. We're 3-6, 2-3 in the MAC. I'm still steaming.

Here's what kills me. This was a game we should have won going away. Our guys forced two fumbles, Gabe Aramboles got one and Mikeah Webster got the other, and we didn't give it away once. Zero giveaways on the road and we still lost. Explain that one.

Explanation: flags. Ten penalties for 95 yards, and Ball State Athletics counted eight of them before halftime, including three straight on one UMass drive that handed them 30 yards and the tying score. Then Brody Boehm hits a 22-yarder to put us up 10-7 with 33 seconds left, and our defense gives up 64 yards in two snaps. Fourteen seconds. Brutal.

Now the good stuff, because there was plenty. Jalen Bonds was a grown man out there. 132 yards on 17 carries, a 42-yard touchdown run in the third and the overtime score from the 1. Ball State Athletics says it's the first 100-yard game of his career. It won't be the last.

And Keldric Luster, down 24-17 in the fourth with 2:14 left, takes us 75 yards in nine plays and walks in from the 2 with 25 seconds to go. That's a quarterback. He finished 17 of 27 for 182 and a touchdown to Jamarion McDougle, the opener from 20 yards out. Sterling Smith had 9 tackles. Webster had 7 and the strip.

But UMass threw for 302, outgained us 455 to 350, and we went 6-14 on third down. That's the game right there, plus one kick.

Buffalo comes to Scheumann Stadium next Wednesday, Nov. 11, 7:30 PM ET. Fill the place. Keep the flags in the pocket, and nobody blinks on the extra point.

articles.title: Massachusetts vs Ball State: Pop Watson Runs It In and the Skid Is Dead
articles.matchup: Final: Ball State Cardinals (3-6) 30, Massachusetts Minutemen (5-4) 31 (OT), Wed., Nov. 4, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst. Next: at Toledo, Wed., Nov. 11, time TBA, Glass Bowl, Toledo
articles.text:
Thirteen yards. That's how far William Watson III had to go in overtime Wednesday night, and he went all of it. Derek Morris put the kick through, and UMass beat Ball State 31-30 at McGuirk. Four straight losses, buried. We're 5-4.

Count the holes we climbed out of. Down 7-0 after one quarter. Down 10-7 with 33 seconds left in the half. Down 17-14 in the third after we coughed up the ball at their end of the field. Every time, this team got back up off the mat. Three deficits, three answers.

The answer before halftime was the best one. Ball State kicks a field goal, Kezion Dia-Johnson brings the kickoff back 28 yards, and two snaps later Watson drops a 64-yarder on Jabari Lewis. Fourteen seconds, 64 yards, 14-10 at the break. That's how you walk into a locker room.

Then the third quarter. Watson hit Harding for 46 and Dia-Johnson for 47 on back-to-back plays, then ran it in himself from the 1. 21-17. Watson finished 17 of 25 for 302 yards, a career high per UMass Athletics. Dia-Johnson had 3 catches for 97. T.Y. Harding caught 6 for 70.

Now the part I'm not happy about. Harding put the ball on the ground twice, and the second one turned into a 42-yard Jalen Bonds touchdown run. Morris missed from 36 on our first drive. And we went up 24-17 with 2:14 left and still let Keldric Luster go 75 yards to tie it with 25 seconds on the clock. Close the door, fellas.

Overtime, though. Ball State scored first and missed the extra point, wide left. That's the opening. Watson took it 12 yards, then 13 more, and the place went nuts. Curtis Kimmons IV gave us 85 hard yards on 19 carries all night, Zeraun Daniel made 10 tackles, and Joshua Iseah sacked Luster twice.

UMass Athletics says five wins is the most for this program since 2011, and the most since the move to FBS. Read that again. Five.

Next Wednesday it's Toledo at the Glass Bowl, and those guys are 7-2. Hold onto the football, make the kicks, and let Pop cook.
